Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

NATIVE ROLE: Reflection Agent

You are an expert research assistant. You will receive a research report (in Markdown) and a newly proposed idea for that report's research problem. Your job is to identify any gaps or issues—such as missing details, logical flaws, or questionable evaluations of novelty, impact, or implementation difficulty.  

- If the report and idea contain all necessary information, do not generate any follow-up questions.  
- If you detect a knowledge gap or something that needs deeper exploration, generate one or more self-contained follow-up queries. Each query must include enough context so that a web search could answer it, For each query, give a short note explaining why you use the query and what you hope it will reveal.
- Focus on technical details, implementation specifics, and any emerging methods or references that were overlooked.  
- Use clear, direct language and avoid unnecessary jargon.

 ## Search results
Recent work supports separating persistent preferences from immediate intent. [MSMT-LSI (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1007/s44196-024-00460-5) combines multitemporal embeddings with separate long-/short-term attention; its evaluation notes weaker performance on sparse Amazon histories, where temporal evidence is limited. [LS4SRec (2025)](https://doi.org/10.1145/3723173) uses independent interest encoders plus a global interaction graph to supply collaborative signals under sparsity. [Dual-frequency self-attention (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ins.2025.122700) explicitly separates low-/high-frequency preference information and adds contrastive learning. These approaches motivate multiple interest timescales, but do not establish gains on the pinned four-category benchmark.

A practical architecture hypothesis: retain SASRec for sequential context, add a recent-window intent encoder and a pooled persistent-interest encoder, then learn a fusion gate conditioned on history length, timestamp gaps and agreement between branches. Timestamp decay should be learned or bucketed; aggressive fixed decay could discard useful evidence in sparse histories. [GDA-REIM (2026)](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neunet.2026.108721) combines gated attention denoising with separate repetition/exploration scoring, suggesting that noise suppression and intent separation can reinforce each other. However, exact-item repetition scoring has limited relevance when recommendations exclude previously seen items; transfer the idea to recurring patterns among unseen candidates. This proposed adaptation is an inference from the literature, requiring controlled ablations of recent pooling, long-term pooling, gating and temporal features using macro validation HR@10.

---

Recent work supports combining sequence representations with shared transition structure. GaGNN (2024) builds individual and group transition graphs, encodes sequential and collaborative information separately, then fuses them—relevant to sparse histories where individual sequences provide weak evidence. This supports testing a training-only transition branch alongside SASRec, although its benefit on the pinned Amazon benchmark remains unverified. [GaGNN](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S002002552400536X)

Text-enhanced graph hybrids exist, but pretrained-model dependence matters. SAGERec (2025) combines a semantic graph, adaptive edge weights and a lightweight Transformer; its graph uses pretrained language representations, making it unsuitable for direct adoption here. The paper also acknowledges that semantic similarity can misrepresent substitutes versus complements. A constraint-compatible experimental alternative: title/description token embeddings learned from scratch, pooled into item features, with gated fusion of ID, text and transition representations. This is a proposed adaptation, not an established result from that paper. [SAGERec](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/24/4844)

Complementarity requires more than similarity. SComGNN (AAAI 2024) models complementary items through both relevance and dissimilarity, using low-pass and mid-pass graph filters with attention. Its findings caution against indiscriminate neighbor averaging. For these interaction-only datasets, directed transitions and lexical similarity should remain separate, uncertain signals: neither establishes functional compatibility or a substitute/complement label. An efficient experiment would use normalized top-k transition neighbors, shallow graph propagation and learned text pooling; compare sequence-only, graph-only additions, text-only additions and their combination using macro validation HR@10. [SComGNN](https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28734)

---

Recent work supports testing SASRec’s loss and negative coverage before adding architecture complexity. [gSASRec’s 2024 extended abstract](https://ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/939) links sampled BCE to overconfidence and proposes generalized BCE; this is distinct from false-negative contamination. [eSASRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.06450) identifies a strong combination of autoregressive training, LiGR layers, and sampled softmax, although its combined improvements do not isolate the loss effect. [Scalable-SASRec (RecSys 2024)](https://github.com/AIRI-Institute/Scalable-SASRec) supplies direct comparisons of multi-negative BCE, generalized BCE, sampled CE, and scalable CE. [LogQ correction research (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) further cautions that the always-present positive requires different treatment from sampled negatives when deriving corrections.

Hard negatives warrant a curriculum and safeguards. [R²NS (WWW 2026)](https://renzhaochun.github.io/assets/pdf/WWW_2026_Camera_Ready.pdf) reports that introducing hard negatives too early can underperform uniform sampling; its approach combines uniform warm-up, global candidate recall, and progressively harder stochastic selection. Sampling among top-ranked candidates reduces reliance on a single potentially false negative, but cannot establish irrelevance. A [2024 sampling comparison](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) also finds dataset-dependent accuracy and popularity tradeoffs. Practical inference for this task: compare baseline BCE against sampled softmax with 16/64/256 negatives, then test a warm-start mixture of uniform and moderately hard negatives. Mask padding, target collisions, and known training positives; use only training histories for these controls. ## Starting Research Idea
SASRec predicts the next item using causal self-attention over a user's interaction history. Learned item and position embeddings feed attention and feed-forward blocks; the resulting sequence representation scores candidate items through embedding dot products. Attention selects relevant recent or distant interactions. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781).
